title: In-Context Learning of Temporal Point Processes with Foundation Inference Models
claim: One pretrained encoder-decoder maps a context of event sequences plus a query history and mark directly to an intensity estimate.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right flow, column headings above, query inputs joining from below
description: A single left-to-right block diagram with column titles: Context Sequences, Transformer, Intensity Estimate, plus History and Mark labels below. On the left, a mint-green rounded box holds stacked event-sequence rasters S^1, S^2, ..., S^m. Each raster has solid and dashed vertical ticks on a time axis. Three gray arrows lead into a rounded box labeled Ψ_enc, which is split into V, K and Q slots. Ψ_enc feeds the V and K slots of a second box, Ψ_dec. A smaller mint box below holds the history H_t with a pink query time t, and it feeds the Q slot of Ψ_dec. The decoder output meets a circle joined with the pink mark κ coming up from below. An arrow then leads to a gray box of blue parameters α, β and μ. A final arrow points down to the intensity λ(t, κ | H_t).
caption: Schematic representation of \FIM. A context of marked event sequences $\contextseq^j$ is encoded by a self-attentive transformer encoder. The result is further processed by a transformer decoder, using a history $\history_t$ of marked events before time $t$ as queries. The final embedding is joined with an encoding of mark $\markel$. The results is projected to a set of parameters that determine the value of the conditional intensity function $\hat{\lambda}$ evaluated at $(t, \markel)$.
abstract: Modeling event sequences of multiple event types with marked temporal point processes (MTPPs) provides a principled way to uncover governing dynamical rules and predict future events. Current neural network approaches to MTPP inference rely on training separate, specialized models for each target system. We pursue a radically different approach: drawing on amortized inference and in-context learning, we pretrain a deep neural network to infer, in-context, the conditional intensity functions of event histories from a context defined by sets of event sequences. Pretraining is performed on a large synthetic dataset of MTPPs sampled from a broad distribution of Hawkes processes. Once pretrained, our Foundation Inference Model for Point Processes (FIM-PP) can estimate MTPPs from real-world data without any additional training, or be rapidly finetuned to target systems. Experiments show that this amortized approach matches the performance of specialized models on next-event prediction across common benchmark datasets.
